catalyst.event: August non-farm payrolls, consensus +45k after July printed -23k; unemployment seen 4.1%->4.2%
catalyst.action: hold existing position into the print; add only on a dip into 82.0-82.6 before Friday, do not chase above 83.6

thesis: UPDATE to the position opened 2026-08-20 at 82.60 (last 82.88, +0.3%) — entry level unchanged, but the reason to hold is now dated. July payrolls were outright negative at -23k and consensus for the Aug 4 Sep print is only +45k with the unemployment rate expected to tick to 4.2%, so a second soft print forces the market to price a larger Fed cut at the September FOMC against an effective funds rate already down to 3.63%. TLT sits at 82.88 on a 10y of 4.67%, near the low end of its 120-day 81.17-88.95 range and only 0.4% above its 20-day SMA of 82.50.
key_risk: Payrolls come in hot (+100k or better) or average hourly earnings reaccelerate; long-end yields are being set by term premium and deficit supply as much as by the funds rate, so TLT can fail to rally even on a weak print. TLT ATR is only 0.70, so the 80.95 stop is under 3 ATR and a single bad auction can reach it.
counter_argument: The 10y-2y curve at +39bp is steepening, which is exactly what happens when the Fed cuts into a deficit-heavy long end: the front end rallies and the 20-year sector does not. If that is the regime, the correct expression of a dovish view is the 2-year, which this account cannot trade, and TLT goes nowhere.

catalyst.event: August non-farm payrolls — consensus +45k after July printed -23k, unemployment seen 4.1%->4.2%. This is the print that decides whether the September hike Warsh floated at Jackson Hole is survivable.
catalyst.action: WAIT. Do not add before Friday. Buy only into 81.20-82.60 after a soft print (sub-25k, or unemployment 4.3%+). If payrolls beat +100k, stand down entirely — this idea is void, not cheaper.

thesis: This REPLACES and downgrades my own earlier capture today, which argued a weak print forces a larger Fed cut — that framing was wrong. Warsh said at Jackson Hole on Aug 28 that underlying inflation trends have not improved and the Fed may have work to do, and CME odds of a September HIKE jumped ~20 points to 55.7%. The trade that survives is narrower: the Fed is signalling a hike into a labour market that shed 23k jobs in July, and a second soft print makes that untenable, which is when the 20-year sector reprices. TLT closed 82.88 with ATR 0.70, near the low end of its 120-day 81.17-88.95 range.
key_risk: This is now a direct bet against what the sitting Fed chair said four days ago, on thin evidence, which is why conviction is 2 and size is 1%. If payrolls firm up, the September hike gets priced toward certain and TLT goes through 80.20 without pausing. Long-end yields also answer to term premium and deficit supply, so TLT can lose even when the front end is right.
counter_argument: The strongest case against: hawkish repricing usually bear-flattens, and with the 10y-2y curve already at +39bp the pain from a hike lands hardest on the short end, not on TLT. Under that reading TLT is neither a good hedge nor a good expression, and the honest answer is that this account cannot trade the instrument that actually expresses the view.

thesis: Update to the position opened 2026-08-22 at 115.00 (last 120.81, +5.0%): hold the core, add only below. LULU trades at 120.81, 38.3% below its 195.74 high of the last 150 sessions, on a quarter management has already told the market will be bad — the guide embeds a 410bp gross margin hit that is mostly tariff, which is a cost shock with an expiry date rather than a demand problem, while China Mainland is still guided to grow mid-to-high teens. The setup is a de-rated brand where the bad news is already in the guidance rather than still to come.
key_risk: INVALIDATION (no hard stop, this is a multi-quarter thesis): North America revenue declines worsen beyond low double digits for two more quarters, or FY2027 guidance fails to show gross margin recovering once the tariff step-up anniversaries. Bear-case price 85 — about 30% below the 104.44 range low, where the market would be pricing structural brand impairment rather than a cost cycle. Near-term risk: the stock has already rallied 15.7% off 104.44 into the print so the low-expectations edge is partly spent, and with a 4.36 ATR (3.6%) a 15% gap either way on Thursday night is normal.
counter_argument: The bear case is that North America is not a tariff problem at all but brand fatigue — low-double-digit US declines are far too steep to blame on price, competitors have taken the category, and China is simply doing now what US growth did before it rolled over. If that is right the multiple keeps compressing and 120 is not cheap, it is early.

catalyst.event: A four-print week that either confirms or kills the September hike: ISM Manufacturing Tue Sep 1 10:00 ET, ADP + Fed Beige Book Wed Sep 2, ISM Services Thu Sep 3 10:00 ET, and August payrolls Fri Sep 4 08:30 ET.
catalyst.action: Short into strength in the 770-776 zone, ideally on a push back toward Friday's 775.30 high early in the week. Cover half at 750. Do not add after the payroll print — the event will already have happened.

thesis: The rates market repriced a September Fed HIKE from roughly 36% to 55.7% on Friday after Warsh said at Jackson Hole that underlying inflation has not improved and the Fed may have work to do. Gold fell 3.2% on its heaviest volume in 120 days and the Russell dropped 1.35%. The S&P fell 0.23% and closed at 769.35, still only 1.29% off its 120-day high of 779.37 and sitting exactly on its 20-day SMA of 769.22, with ATR14 at 0.66% — near the bottom of its realised-volatility range. Equities have not marked the same news the bond and gold markets marked.
key_risk: Shorting an index 1.3% below its high is the most common way to lose money, and the 782 stop is only 1.7 ATR above entry, so an ordinary drift higher takes it out. The hedge is also two-sided on the catalyst: a weak Friday payroll print kills the hike, and the market may read that as bullish before it reads it as recessionary.
counter_argument: Warsh explicitly gave no forward guidance and no reaction function, and stopped well short of signalling a September move — 55.7% is a coin flip, not a decision. With July payrolls at -23k and unemployment heading to 4.2%, a hike may simply not happen, in which case the honest read is that equities were right to shrug and the bond and gold moves were the overreaction.

catalyst.event: FDA PDUFA action date for UX111 (rebisufligene etisparvovec), an AAV9 gene therapy seeking accelerated approval in Sanfilippo syndrome type A — a fatal pediatric lysosomal storage disease with no approved treatment. BLA resubmission was accepted Apr 2, 2026.
catalyst.action: Accumulate 24.60-25.80 over the next week. Trim half into the Sep 18 close so the remaining position is the only thing exposed to the binary — do not hold full size through the action date.

thesis: The July 2025 complete response letter on UX111 was explicitly CMC-only — additional chemistry, manufacturing and controls information plus facility inspection observations — not efficacy or safety, so the FDA has already accepted the clinical case for accelerated approval. The specific de-risking event the market appears not to have credited: on Aug 19, 2026 the FDA approved GENGLYCOS, Ultragenyx's first gene therapy and its fifth approval overall, which means the agency has recently inspected and cleared this company's gene-therapy manufacturing — the exact thing the CRL was about. RARE trades at 25.61, 30% below its 150-day high of 36.57 and below both its 20-day (26.02) and 50-day (28.43) averages, drifting lower into the date.
key_risk: Cash burn is the real problem, not the science: Ultragenyx lost $92M in Q2 and $277M in H1 2026, with $294M of operating cash burn in the half against 2026 revenue guidance of $730-760M. A second CRL, or an equity raise on the back of an approval, are both live and would swamp the catalyst. Note also that this stock sells its own good news — on Aug 20, the session after the GENGLYCOS approval, it opened at 28.39 and closed at 25.32 on the heaviest volume of the month.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the Aug 20 fade was the market telling you something true: an accelerated approval in an ultra-rare fatal pediatric disease is worth very little revenue against a $294M half-year burn, so approval may be the moment the financing arrives rather than the moment the stock re-rates. The setrusumab Phase 3 failure in December 2025 also showed how fast this name can lose 40% on a single binary.

catalyst.action: Let it come to you into 282-298. Do not buy while it is still making lower lows — require a daily close above the prior session high inside the zone. Exit into the print or hold a half for the FY27 guide, but do not add above 305.

thesis: JBL closed 301.45, roughly 30% below the 428.93 intraday high of the last 150 sessions and far under its converged 20- and 50-day averages at 333.75 and 334.08, after falling about 18% in five consecutive sessions in late August including -8.45% on Aug 18. Nothing in the fundamentals moved with it: guidance was raised, not cut, and AI revenue is guided to $13.6B in FY2026 from $9B in FY2025 with FY2027 growth at a similar rate and margin above 6%. At 301.45 against $12.70 of guided FY2026 core EPS that is about 23.7x, versus the roughly 30x it carried at its $385.55 closing high on Jun 15, 2026 on guidance that has since improved. The trade is mean reversion to the 334 shelf into a dated event that puts FY2027 numbers on the table.
key_risk: **I could not establish why the stock fell 18% in five sessions, and that is the reason this is a conviction 2 at 1% rather than a standard position.** Coverage attributes it to profit-taking with guidance intact, but an unexplained waterfall in a $32B name usually has a holder or a customer behind it, and a contract manufacturer's biggest single risk is a large customer insourcing. The 272 stop is only 1.4 ATR below entry on a 4.64% ATR stock, so it is genuinely exposed to noise.
counter_argument: The strongest case against: JBL is an EMS business trading at an AI multiple, and the market may simply be starting to price the end of the capex cycle before the numbers show it. If that is right, the correct multiple is closer to 15x — under 200 — and every level in this trade is a step on the way down. That is also why I rejected the long-term version of this idea, which cannot clear a 2.5 floor against that bear case.

catalyst.event: A physical generation-equipment shortage with a multi-year order book behind it. Gas Power equipment backlog plus slot reservation agreements went from 100 GW to 116 GW in Q2 2026 with at least 125 GW guided by year-end; total backlog is $176B; the company is scaling annual gas turbine output from 20 GW in Q3 2026 to 24 GW in 2028 and 30 GW in 2030. Behind it: US datacenter electricity demand went from 23 GW in 2023 to 42 GW in 2026 with 75.8 GW projected, against grid interconnection queues of 5-7 years and 7-10 in the best markets.
catalyst.action: Accumulate in thirds into 780-840 as the drawdown continues. Do not start at 912 — it closed Friday at 911.93, one tick off the session low of 911.33, on the ninth down day out of ten. Add a further third on any macro-driven flush under 750. No urgency; the backlog is booked into 2029.

thesis: GE Vernova sells the specific thing that is scarce. The binding constraint on AI datacenter buildout is no longer capital or chips but delivered electrons, and GEV's turbine slots are the bottleneck — its Q2 2026 orders were $24.2B, up 88% organically, revenue $11.1B up 22%, free cash flow $5.1B in the quarter, and it raised 2026 revenue and free cash flow guidance. The stock is nonetheless 23.8% below its 150-day high of 1195.94 at 911.93 and far under its 50-day average of 1031.65, because the whole AI-power complex was sold on a thesis-level fear of capex overbuild rather than on any company news — NRG is 41.5% off its high and sits 0.42% above its 150-day low, VST is 23.1% off, PWR 23.6%, CEG 17.1%. Vistra's Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose 31% year over year while its stock fell 37% from its high, which is the cleanest evidence available that this is a multiple de-rating and not an earnings event.
key_risk: INVALIDATION (long-term thesis, no hard stop): the gas power equipment backlog plus slot reservations fail to reach the guided 125 GW by year-end 2026, or decline in any quarter, or the 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guide of 12-14% is cut. Either would mean the order book is being cancelled or cannot be built profitably, which is the actual thesis. Bear-case price 690 — a capex-cycle roll that takes it back toward the 656.00 low of the last 150 sessions. Concrete near-term evidence for that risk already exists: Q2 adjusted EPS was $2.47 against a $3.04 consensus, an 18.75% miss, so converting this backlog into earnings is visibly not going smoothly.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that hyperscalers are ordering turbine slots the way they ordered GPUs — as option value, not as committed capacity — and slot reservations are not firm orders. If AI capex payback periods disappoint, reservations get released, the 116 GW converts at a far lower rate than the market assumed, and GEV is a cyclical industrial that was priced as a secular compounder. The 18.75% EPS miss alongside record orders is exactly the shape that argument would take early.

thesis: DG round-tripped a beat-and-raise in 48 hours. It gapped to about 134 pre-market on Aug 27 (+9%), closed that session at 125.89, and closed Friday at 122.89 — below the 122.78 it closed at the day before the print. Nothing in the numbers deteriorated in between: the comp was traffic-led at +2.0%, which is customers rather than price, and full-year EPS guidance was raised by roughly 8% at the midpoint. At 122.89 against $7.90 of guided FY2026 EPS that is 15.6x, and the stock is 22.3% below its 158.23 high of the last 150 sessions, sitting on its 50-day average of 121.30. The macro behind it is the same labour data that threatens the rest of the book — July payrolls at -23k and unemployment heading to 4.2% is the environment where a traffic-driven discounter takes share, and DG outperformed Dollar Tree on the same day.
key_risk: The market may have faded the print for a reason: the gross margin expansion could be a temporary shrink-and-markdown benefit rather than a structural gain, in which case the guidance raise does not repeat and 15.6x is the right multiple, not a cheap one. A genuinely strong Sep 4 payroll number also removes the trade-down tailwind. The 113.50 stop is 1.9 ATR below entry on a 3.23% ATR name.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this is the third time in ten days this report has pointed at DG, and the level has barely moved — at some point that is anchoring rather than patience. The honest answer is that the Aug 27 print is the concrete new information the repetition guard asks for, but it also means the previously published 119.00 entry was set on worse information than exists now.

thesis: This is a deliberate minority position and it is sized like one. Barclays now expects 25bp hikes in both September and December, and the market implies 57.5% for September, so being long duration here is fighting a well-supported consensus. The disagreement is specific: the Fed is proposing to hike into a labour market that shed 23k jobs in July with unemployment heading to 4.2%, and hiking cycles do not usually begin on negative payroll prints. If August is soft too, the September hike becomes untenable and the 20-year sector reprices. TLT closed 82.88 with ATR 0.70 against a 120-day range of 81.17-88.95, so the entry now sits at the bottom of that range rather than in the middle of it — the risk went up, so the price I will pay went down.
key_risk: Two hikes is now the sell-side baseline, not a tail. Long-end yields also answer to term premium and deficit supply rather than the funds rate, so TLT can lose even if the no-hike call is right. **This is the position whose original thesis today's news broke — it was opened on 2026-08-20 at 82.60 when a cut was the base case, and there is no cut on the table any more. Holders should treat the invalidation as nearer than the 79.60 stop implies and should not average down into it.** Conviction 2 and 1% reflect that this is one contrarian read on four days of evidence.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is mechanical: a hawkish repricing bear-flattens, and with the 10y-2y curve at only +39bp the damage from a hiking cycle lands on the front end, not the 20-year. Under that reading TLT is neither a good hedge nor a good expression of the view, and the instrument that would actually express it — the 2-year — is not tradeable in this account. A reader who accepts that argument should simply close the existing position rather than add.
